note: Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain), fetched into runs/theory-tests/<job>/answers.jsonl. These are the only files in either S3 job folder. When I opened them, all 328 rows in each file had no n_tok_p_lt_1e2 key, and no row had n_tok_p_lt_1e3, min_token_logprob or attempt either. The inventory lists the field for these jobs, but only the later min-p jobs (round-05 inventory, SPEC_minp.md) write it. So the script should print not_computable, and it does not switch to another file or field. Under the literal drop rule ('drop if missing') every problem would be dropped, leaving 0/0, which gives the same result. If the field is present when the script runs, it computes the recipe as written. With no attempt field it keeps the first row per problem_index in file order (no index repeats). 'Finished' means cap_hit is false in both files. Rate is pooled sum t / sum n_generated, RL over base. Other reading (alt_measured): n_new as the denominator, as egate.py does (n_generated = n_new + 1 in these rows). The bootstrap resamples paired problems. example_row leaves out text and prompt.

File: e72c answers.jsonl (base cue) only. n_tok_p_lt_1e2 does not exist in any of its 328 rows (see k=1), so the script should print not_computable. Otherwise it follows the recipe. Right means score_v3 == 1, and anything else is wrong (no score_v3 is null in the file). Rows are sorted by (n_generated, problem_index) and q = floor(4r/N). A quartile is skipped if it has no wrong rows, no right rows, or rR == 0. The statistic is the mean of ratio_q weighted by the number of wrong rows. Other reading (alt_measured): the unweighted mean of ratio_q over the kept quartiles. The bootstrap reassigns quartiles inside each resample, and duplicate rows get consecutive ranks. If a resample skips all four quartiles it returns NaN, which would break the percentile sort (unlikely with about 300 rows).

Files: e72c and 86ef answers.jsonl as in k=1. n_tok_p_lt_1e2 is absent from every row of both files, so the script should print not_computable. Tension: read literally, the drop rule removes every problem, both groups become empty, and the recipe would then count that as refuted. I treat a field that no row has as not computable, not as an empty group, because the empty-group clause is about how the data falls, not about a field that was never stored. A reviewer might instead score this as refuted_without_number. If the field is present: keep problems where base cap_hit is false and score_v3 != 1 and RL cap_hit is false, apply the null/zero drop, set d = ln((t_RL+0.5)/g_RL) - ln((t_b+0.5)/g_b), fixed = RL score_v3 == 1, statistic = mean d(fixed) - mean d(unfixed). An empty group gives refuted_without_number. Other reading (alt_measured): n_new instead of n_generated as g. The bootstrap resamples paired problems. A resample with an empty group returns NaN (unlikely).
